newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee firm in convertibility report's shadow.
newsitem.headline: India rupee firm in convertibility report's shadow.

text.p: The Indian rupee quietly firmed on Tuesday, uunaffected by all the attention focussed on an report mapping out the route to capital account convertibility by the end of the century.
The rupee closed at 35.7850/7950 to the dollar, firming from an open at 35.80/81 which was unahcnged from Monday.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made no intervention to curb the rupee's strength after its aggressive dollar buying on Monday.
"You wouldn't expect them (the RBI) to show up the day they were releasing a report on convertibility (of the rupee)," a dealer at a leading brokerage said.
The report charts a roadmap for achieving full capital account convertibility in three years.
The release of the report in the afternoon had minimal impact on trading, dealers said.
"The October premium went up by one paise, but it immediately reverted," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Forward premiums continued to seek lower levels, tracking an easing of overnight call money rates.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 4.30 percent compared to the previous close of 4.36 percent.
Dealers said the RBI was constrained from intervening regularly because the consequent expansion in money supply would undermine its M3 growth target cap of 15.5 percent for the year.
India's year-on-year M3 growth rose to 16.3 percent on May 9, according to latest data from the RBI.
Some dealers said they expected RBI to shift its dollar purchases from the spot to the forward market with a view to postponing the injection of rupees into the banking system.
